# Art deco recipe

Concept: a 1930s poster that moves. Warm lacquer, engraved gold line, airbrushed hard-edged volumes. A sunburst is the ground, a stepped title bar opens out of two gold keylines, a bulb sign lights letter by letter, the camera tilts down a lit tower, an ivory invitation is held in a gloved hand, and each scene change is a door. Everything hangs on one vertical axis (x 960) and moves like machinery: symmetric, from the centre, counted, crane-smooth.

Register: glamour against a ticking clock. Opening night, launch, deadline, promise kept.

## Rules of the look
- Ornament is the content. Sunburst = background, stepped arches and ziggurats = frames, clock = progress bar, bulb sign = reveal, door = transition.
- One saturated colour exists, and only the protagonist (a figure or the single object the story follows) wears it. All else is gold, lacquer, ivory.
- Not gold-foil clip art: things need volume, light and motion.
- Rule out Art Nouveau: whiplash curves and flowers stay out.
- Rule out the flat vector poster: every volume gets airbrush shading and a gold rim.
- Rule out the 60s spy title: no silhouettes cut from flat colour.
- Not a luxury template: no glitter, no lens flare, no serif-on-black with a fade.

## Surfaces and materials
Ground: warm lacquer black. Never grey-black, never `#000`. Night sky leans navy at the top and deep emerald at the horizon.

Sunburst: 44 wedge pairs fanning from one point just below the title bar. Pitch 8.2 degrees, light wedge takes 46% of it. Fill each light wedge with a radial gradient, 22% gold over the ground at the centre down to 10% at the rim. Edge it with a gold hairline that fades out near the centre so rays do not knot. Draw once; do not rotate.

Gold is banded metal: dark (gold 50% toward black), body, hot (gold 42% toward warm white), body, dark. Use it on doors, lamp posts, the seal, sliding leaves. On type, apply it as a background-clipped gradient and sweep the hot band across for the sheen.

Keyline: 3 px gold stroke plus a 1.6 px twin 8 px inside. Put it on title bar, subtitle card, plaque, medallion. Fill every panel with the lacquer second surface so rays never cross text.

Stepped forms:
- Frame: rectangle whose short ends step outward twice, at 20% and 36% of its height.
- Ziggurat: three nested stepped lines, each step 62 x 62 px, running from under the title bar to the bottom edge.
- Arches: semicircles of radius 285, 215 and 100 (at 1920 wide) standing on the bar.

Architecture, in real perspective:
- Tower tapers upward, half-width 410 to 470 px over its height, so the tilt reads as a low angle. Windows sit between converging gold pilasters.
- Lobby: one-point perspective, vanishing point (960, 560). Side walls airbrushed gold, pilasters shrinking with depth, a chevron runner leading to the door.

Bulb sign: outline letters, 2.5 px gold stroke, filled with a 13 px grid of bulbs. Unlit bulbs are dim gold dots on lacquer. Lit bulbs are hot-gold dots on the gold-word colour, each letter with a soft radial halo behind it.

Invitation card: ivory, double keyline set 26 px in, ink type, one gold rule, one line in the protagonist colour mixed into ink, a gold seal, a small emerald fan stamp in the corner. Soft drop shadow, no glow.

Characters: tall, tapered, airbrushed planes, gold rim on the lit (left) side, seen from behind or in profile, no facial detail. The default is an usher in the brand colour, pillbox hat, white gloves.

Light: lamps and doors throw a radial gold pool, 55% at the centre fading to 0. Card-scene bokeh is a few dozen soft gold discs drifting upward.

## Colour tokens
- `--latar`: lacquer ground and night-sky base. Sky = 20% navy over it; horizon = 12% emerald.
- `--latar-2`: any panel behind type (title bar, subtitle card, plaque, medallion, canopy) and the lit side of the facade (12% toward gold).
- `--aksen`: the gold. Keylines (`--aksen` 86% toward `--teks`, so they darken on light brands and lighten on dark), metal bands, lit windows, bulbs, doors, lamp posts, seal, sliding leaves, sunburst wedges.
- `--aksen-di-latar`: gold words on ground or panel. Title sheen = gradient of it with a band 48% toward `--teks`. A light brand therefore gets dark, readable titles.
- `--utama`: the one colour. Usher jacket and hat, the sleeve of the gloved hand, and one card line (56% with ink so it reads on ivory in any brand). Nothing else saturated.
- `--teks`: subtitles; stars and moon (82% with gold); light stripes of the lobby runner (88% over ground).
- `--teks-redup`: small notes. `--teks-di-utama` and `--teks-di-aksen`: labels sitting on the protagonist colour or a gold plaque.
- Fixed in every brand: paper `#eee4cf`, ink `#1c140b`, emerald stamp `#2f6b55`, skin `#b9845e`, trousers `#232036`.
- Light brand: becomes a gold-on-ivory invitation. White ground, darker keylines, gold words fall back to dark text, runner flips to dark chevrons.
- Dark brand (navy): keeps the night. Accent becomes the metal, main colour becomes the protagonist.
- Reference palette: ground `#0b0906`, gold `#c9a35e`, ivory `#eee4cf`, ink `#1c140b`, crimson `#b8364a`, card line burgundy (crimson mixed with ink), emerald `#2f6b55`.

## Type
`--font-judul` (architectural): Limelight.
- 92 px on the title bar (cap height ~65 px, bar 1040 x 220)
- 60 px on the plaque
- 136 px in ink on the card
- 176 px for bulb-sign outlines, letter-spacing 0.08em
- 40 px stacked medallion numerals, line height 52 px

`--font-isi` (labels, subtitles): Poppins 500.
- Tracked caps 40 px, letter-spacing 0.3em, plus equal padding-left to stay centred on the axis
- Subtitles 44 px, sentence case
- Card colour line 54 px, tracking 0.18em

No brand fonts? Limelight for titles. Quieter bookish deco: Cormorant Garamond 700. Silent-film card: IM Fell English. Labels: Poppins 500 or Inter 600; Oswald 500 for a condensed newsreel tag. Skip Bebas Neue and similar modern condensed sans; they read as sport.

Title rules: sits on a stepped bar or plaque, centred on the axis, one line. For a wider brand font keep to about 14 characters on the 1040 px bar. Never shrink under 80 px.
Density: max 7 words on screen beside the subtitle; subtitle card holds one line.

## Timing and motion
Open from the centre: point, hairline, panel.
- Title bar: two keylines 14 px apart grow from 60% to full width (0.3 s). They split to +-103 px while a clip-path opens the panel from 47% inset to 0 (0.45 s, power3.inOut). Title rises from yPercent 110 (0.5 s, expo.out), 0.27 s after the split begins. Label follows 0.2 s after the title.
- Subtitle cards and plaque: open sideways from the centre in 0.42 s. Text rises 24 px, 0.24 s later.
- Draw-on: gold strokes engrave outward from the centre (arches from the top, stairs from under the bar). 0.8 s power2.out, 0.03 s stagger.
- Ornament order: medallion scales 0.4 to 1, back.out(1.4), 0.45 s. Its 17 crown ticks grow from the medallion centre, 0.025 s apart, middle outward. Wings extend from the bar edges in 0.5 s. Date line rises last. Title is complete at about 1.9 s and holds. Sheen crosses once (0.8 s, power1.inOut).
- Counted light: one letter per 0.2 s. Each lit layer switches on in 0.05 s; its halo flashes to full and settles to 45% in 0.18 s. After the last letter, run a chase through the halos (0.06 s apart, 0.08 s up and down). Tower windows light in a seeded random order over 2.4 s, 0.08 s each.
- Machinery: firm ease-in-out with a small settle.
  - Split door: gold seam draws down the axis (0.3 s); each leaf then narrows to its outer hinge, scaleX 1 to 0, 0.85 s power2.inOut, shaded darker toward the seam.
  - Sliding leaves: shut 0.35 s power2.in, hold 0.1 s, open 0.38 s power3.inOut.
  - Revolving door: whole shot narrows to its left hinge, 0.5 s power2.in.
  - Clock hands: 0.55 s back.out(1.2).
- Frame rate split: camera, light, draw-on and sheen run on ones. Characters run at 12 fps, `steps(12 × duration)`. Walk of 1.3 s = `steps(16)`; sway +-2 degrees at `steps(3)` per 0.26 s; the card in the gloved hand floats 12 px over 2 s at `steps(24)`.
- Holds: title complete for 1.3 s before the doors open; card about 1.8 s after the seal lands; ending at least 2 s, fully still.
- The axis never moves. Symmetry can open or rotate but never drifts off-centre.

## Camera and transitions
- Split: seam on the axis, then two leaves hinged at the frame edges swing off (0.85 s). A threshold crossed. Use for a new place, new chapter, reveal behind a facade.
- Slide: gold leaves close over live action, then open on the next shot (0.35 + 0.1 + 0.38 s). A door shutting on a moment. Use for room to room, a decision made, outside to invitation.
- Revolve: the whole shot swings off its left hinge, accelerating (0.5 s). The next room was right behind. Use for arriving inside, call to action, last chapter.
- Tower tilt: world travels two frame heights in 3 s, power2.inOut, stars at 0.04 parallax. Sign in the sky down to door on the ground. Use for a building from sign to entrance, levels top-down, an arrival.
- Push-in on a dial, medallion or clock; its figure drives the story. Use for a deadline, count, milestone, opening hour.
- Lobby dolly (scale 1.1 to 1, 0.65 s): stepping inside. Venue, welcome, ending with name and contact.
- Extreme low-angle poster tilt: scale and aspiration. A distant goal, tower, monument, launch.
- Architectural section (pull out to a cutaway): progress through a structure. Staged process, company floors, a climb.
- Overhead kaleidoscope, mirrored and turning: people become pattern. Team, release, celebration, system of parts.
- Shape match-cut (sunburst to clock, arch to arch): two places, one rhyme. Departments, cities, eras.
- Pull back, detail to skyline: locates the moment in its city. Aftermath, citywide effect, scale.

Framing: the axis is sacred; an asymmetric frame resolves onto it within the shot. In wide shots the protagonist is small (about a fifth of frame height at the entrance) yet is the only saturated thing, so the eye lands on it. Allowed transitions: splits, slides, revolves, arch openings, shape matches. Never a dissolve or a generic slide.

## Signature moves
- Centre-out title bar. Keylines meet on the axis, split, open a stepped lacquer bar; title rises, wings extend, a numbered medallion lands below, a sheen crosses the gold. For: a gala name, a new series title, a class chapter card, a story title page.
- Counted light. Bulb sign, one letter per beat, ignition flash, then a chase. For: a shop's grand opening, a launch countdown, a channel milestone, a town lighting up as the train pulls in.
- Tilt down the tower. Sign in the night sky, down a lit facade with windows switching on, to a stepped portal where the protagonist arrives. For: a hotel, office or restored cinema roof to door; a course from advanced to basics; a building's history floor by floor; a story's arrival scene.
- Threshold doors. Cut scenes only with doors. For: company departments, class modules, museum rooms, renovation before/after.
- The invitation. Ivory card with double keyline, held by a gloved hand; gold rule engraves itself; seal stamped, then glints. For: a ticket with its price, a webinar invite, a course certificate, a letter that changes a life.
- Dials carry the plot. Clock, floor indicator or gauge replaces narration and settles with a mechanical overshoot. For: an event's opening hour, a funding target filling, flash-sale minutes, a story deadline.
- The one colour. A single figure or object holds the brand colour in a gold and lacquer world. For: the usher who leads us in, one product among rivals, the new student, the hero of a mystery.

## Pitfalls
- Live-preview cost. No CSS `perspective` or 3D rotation around full-frame scenes: measured, it made every frame about five times dearer even at rest. Do door swings in 2D (scaleX from the hinge plus a shade). Switch scenes by `display` only inside their window, turning one on slightly early beneath the previous scene so first paint misses the transition; a `visibility: hidden` full-frame layer still costs. Paint sunburst, tower and lobby once and move whole layers. Searchlights and stars get their own layers. Light windows via opacity on small rects. Halos are radial gradients, never `filter: blur`. Split leaves are two clones of the title scene driven by class; show the second only when the split starts.
- Bulbs come from text: outline stroke plus a background-clipped dot pattern. Hundreds of SVG circles per letter cost frames and fail on curves.
- Pure black: a gold hairline on `#000` looks like a broken frame. Keep lacquer warm and lifted; give the rays a faint fill.
- Gold type on a light brand must use `--aksen-di-latar`, never fixed gold, or it vanishes on white. Check the tower as well: on white the facade is pale and only gold lines and windows draw it.
- Off-centre drift: letter-spaced labels slide right unless padded left by the same amount. Titles, medallions, portals and the vanishing point all sit at x 960.
- No curling stems or flowers. A fish-scale motif must overlap row over row with an inner arc, or it reads as brickwork.
- Pasted-in characters: keep deco proportions (tall, tapered, airbrushed, gold rim), from behind, stepping on twos. Never animate limbs per frame.
- No crossfades, no side slides. Each scene change is a door on the axis.
- Crowding: one title per bar, one subtitle line per card, at most 7 words besides, no label under 40 px.

## Reference numbers
Rhythm of a 12 s film:
- 0-3.3 s title card (complete by 1.5 s)
- 3.3-4.0 s door split
- 4.0-8.3 s night sign and tower tilt (sign 1 s, tilt ~3 s, entrance 1 s)
- 8.3-10.4 s invitation card, held still
- 10.4-10.6 s revolving door into the lobby
- then lobby to the end

The 15 s example scales this by 1.25 and holds the lobby 2.1 s.

Layout: title bar = 50% of frame width, 20% of height, centred at 40% height. Arches sit above it. Sunburst centre at 56% height, medallion at 65%, date line at 77%. Subtitle card = 80% width, 8% height, bottom edge at 91%. Sky = 20% navy over the ground. Card = about 60% of frame width, tilted 2-3 degrees.

## Variation space
Free to choose: structure, characters (or none), setting, opening, ending, and what gets counted.
- Structures:
  - Exhibition: pavilions of a fair, each door hiding one idea.
  - Ocean liner: three decks from engine room up to ballroom.
  - Trophy night: nominees as sunburst panels, the winner picked out by light.
- Openings:
  - Machine room: gold gears and pistons build toward the first beat.
  - Engraved map: a gold route is traced over a map before any figure shows.
  - Telegram: ticker tape types out the premise.
- Endings:
  - Lights out: letters go dark in reverse order, one bulb left burning.
  - Dawn: lacquer black warms into a pale sky.
  - Poster: the closing shot flattens to a printed poster carrying a date.

# Art deco: beat plan

Default length 15 s. Tempo per beat (seconds): short 2.2, medium 3.2, long 4.8.

## hook

- en: a stepped gold title bar unfolds from two keylines at the centre over a sunburst; the title rises, a medallion lands, a sheen sweeps
- id: papan judul emas berundak membuka dari dua garis di tengah, di atas sinar matahari; judul naik, medali mendarat, kilap menyapu

## problem

- en: the bulb sign goes dark letter by letter until one bulb is left; a stopped clock or an unlit door holds the trouble
- id: lampu huruf padam satu per satu sampai tersisa satu bohlam; jam yang berhenti atau pintu gelap menahan masalahnya

## fact

- en: doors split on the centre seam onto a night scene; the camera tilts down a lit tower, the fact on a stepped subtitle bar
- id: pintu membelah di garis tengah ke adegan malam; kamera turun menyusuri menara bercahaya, faktanya di bilah takarir berundak

## step

- en: one floor per step: the camera tilts down the tower and each floor's windows light as its step is named
- id: satu lantai tiap langkah: kamera turun menyusuri menara, jendela tiap lantai menyala saat langkahnya disebut

## compare

- en: two arched doors side by side on the axis; the better one lights gold while the other stays lacquer dark
- id: dua pintu berlengkung berdampingan di sumbu tengah; yang lebih baik menyala emas, yang lain tetap gelap

## number

- en: a clock or dial medallion swings to the figure and settles like a machine; bulbs count it out one per beat
- id: medali jam atau penunjuk berayun ke angkanya lalu berhenti seperti mesin; bohlam menghitungnya satu per ketukan

## proof

- en: an ivory card held up by a gloved hand: the quote or award in black deco type, a gold seal stamped and glinting
- id: kartu gading diangkat tangan bersarung: kutipan atau penghargaan berhuruf deco hitam, segel emas dicap lalu berkilap

## offer

- en: gold doors slide shut and open on an ivory invitation: the name in deco type, a gold rule, the price under it
- id: pintu emas menutup lalu membuka ke kartu undangan gading: nama berhuruf deco, garis emas, harga di bawahnya

## cta

- en: a revolving door turns onto a symmetric lobby: name on a gold plaque over the portal, contact in the subtitle bar, held 2 s
- id: pintu putar membuka lobi simetris: nama di plakat emas di atas gapura, kontak di bilah takarir, diam 2 detik

## payoff

- en: pull back to the lit façade, every bulb of the sign burning and a sheen across the title, held 2 s
- id: kamera mundur ke fasad yang menyala, semua bohlam papan nama hidup, kilap menyapu judul, diam 2 detik
